primary_sources: The Effective Engineer Framework by Edmond Lau

rules.explanation: Spending initial weeks passively waiting for instructions without proactive environment setup or code exploration delays tangible contributions.
rules.do: Master the development environment, review existing codebase documentation independently, and deliver small bug fixes or features within the first two weeks.
rules.dont: Do not remain entirely passive during onboarding or hesitate to ask clarifying questions when blocked.

rules.rule_name: Proactive Seeking of Mentorship and Feedback
rules.explanation: Working in isolation for days without seeking guidance when stuck wastes team resources and slows personal technical growth.
rules.do: Establish regular syncs with assigned mentors, come prepared with specific technical blockers tried independently, and actively request constructive code reviews.
rules.dont: Do not suffer in silence on technical blocks for hours without attempting structured debugging or reaching out to senior engineers.

rules.rule_name: Effective Communication of Technical Progress and Blockers
rules.explanation: Failing to communicate project delays or technical roadblocks until deadlines arrive destroys team trust and project planning.
rules.do: Provide clear, transparent updates on task progress, proactively flag potential roadblocks early, and propose alternative solutions.
rules.dont: Do not hide missed deadlines or unexpected technical hurdles until the final hour of delivery.

rules.explanation: Keeping solved setup hurdles or system discoveries strictly to oneself misses opportunities to elevate team knowledge and demonstrate ownership.
rules.do: Document newly learned troubleshooting steps, setup quirks, and architectural insights into the team wiki or project documentation for future engineers.
rules.dont: Do not hoard troubleshooting knowledge or leave team documentation outdated after resolving complex system issues.
